collection.label: Berossus, History of Babylonia
collection.author_name: Berossus of Babylon (c. 290 BCE), in George Syncellus and Josephus
collection.critical_edition: C. Müller, FHG II and IV (via DFHG, proofread); B. Niese 1889 (Perseus)
collection.search_terms: berossus berosus babyloniaca oannes annedotus xisouthros xisuthrus flood deluge antediluvian kings sar chaldean babylon syncellus nebuchadnezzar
collection.description: The Babylonian priest Berossus' Greek history of his land (c. 290 BCE): Oannes the fish-man who taught civilization, the creation, the ten kings before the flood and the flood of Xisouthros, and the last kings of Babylon, on the pages of a Paris manuscript of George Syncellus and a Florence manuscript of Josephus.

texts.title: Berossus, Babyloniaka book 1: Oannes and the creation (Alexander Polyhistor in George Syncellus)
texts.source: Paris gr. 1711 (George Syncellus, 11th c.) via Gallica + Greek of C. Müller, FHG (DFHG, proofread) + English of I. P. Cory, Ancient Fragments (1832)
texts.description: Berossus' account, as summarized by Alexander Polyhistor and copied by George Syncellus, of the records kept at Babylon, the fish-man Oannes who taught writing, cities, laws and agriculture, and the creation of the world by Bel from the body of Omoroka, shown on the two pages of Paris gr. 1711 that carry it.

texts.title: Berossus, Babyloniaka book 2: the ten kings and the flood of Xisouthros (Alexander Polyhistor in George Syncellus)
texts.source: Paris gr. 1711 (George Syncellus, 11th c.) via Gallica + Greek of C. Müller, FHG (DFHG, proofread) + English of I. P. Cory, Ancient Fragments (1832)
texts.description: Berossus on the ten kings who reigned 120 sars (432,000 years) before the flood and on Xisouthros, warned by Kronos in a dream, who buried the writings at Sippar, built a ship, sent out birds and was taken to live with the gods, shown on the two pages of Paris gr. 1711 that carry it.

texts.title: The tower of Babel in Alexander Polyhistor (the Sibyl) and Abydenus (George Syncellus)
texts.source: Paris gr. 1711 (George Syncellus, 11th c.) via Gallica + Greek of C. Müller, FHG (DFHG, proofread) + English of I. P. Cory, Ancient Fragments (1832)
texts.description: Two Greek accounts of the tower of Babylon copied by George Syncellus from the Babylonian tradition: Alexander Polyhistor quoting the Sibyl on a single language, a tower to heaven overthrown by winds, and Titan and Prometheus after the flood; and Abydenus on the first men, proud of their strength, whose tower was thrown down by the winds and who were given many languages, shown on the page of Paris gr. 1711 that carries them.

texts.title: Berossus in Apollodorus: the ten kings before the flood and the fish-men Annedotoi (George Syncellus)
texts.source: Paris gr. 1711 (George Syncellus, 11th c.) via Gallica + Greek of C. Müller, FHG (DFHG, proofread) + English of I. P. Cory, Ancient Fragments (1832)
texts.description: Apollodorus' list, from Berossus, of the ten Chaldean kings from Aloros to Xisouthros with their reigns in sars, and of the fish-men (Oannes, the Annedotoi, Odakon) who came up from the Red Sea, shown on the two pages of Paris gr. 1711 that carry it.

texts.title: Berossus in Abydenus: the kings of the Chaldeans and the flood of Sisithros (George Syncellus)
texts.source: Paris gr. 1711 (George Syncellus, 11th c.) via Gallica + Greek of C. Müller, FHG (DFHG, proofread) + English of I. P. Cory, Ancient Fragments (1832)
texts.description: Abydenus' retelling of Berossus in Ionic Greek: Aloros the shepherd of the people, the sar of 3,600 years, the Annedotoi who came up from the sea, and Sisithros, who hid the writings at Sippar and sailed to Armenia, shown on the page of Paris gr. 1711 that carries it.

texts.title: Berossus in Josephus, Against Apion 1.128-153: Nabopolassar, Nebuchadnezzar and the last kings of Babylon
texts.source: Florence, Laur. Plut. 69.22 (10th c.) via BML Teca Digitale IIIF + Niese Greek (Perseus) + Whiston English (Project Gutenberg)
texts.description: Josephus quotes Berossus' third book on Nebuchadnezzar's campaign, his building of Babylon and the hanging garden, and the kings after him down to Nabonidus and the capture of Babylon by Cyrus, shown on the four pages of the 10th-century Florence manuscript Laur. Plut. 69.22 that carry it.

authors.name: Berossus
authors.bio: Priest of Bel at Babylon who wrote a history of Babylonia in Greek (the Babyloniaka) for Antiochus I; it survives only in quotations by later writers.
